lines.english: Yes, when it comes to learning, that one offers more. But I want to start saving early and ease the family's burden.

lines.speaker: M
lines.traditional: 家裡的事妳不用擔心。不論妳去哪一家，爸爸都沒意見。只是剛進職場，別只顧著看薪水。

lines.traditional: 他個性開朗，常說笑話逗同學開心，大家都喜歡跟他在一起。

lines.english: Don't rush to criticize him. Children who are scolded a lot tend to fear maths even more. However much homework there is, just check it through with him once a day.

passage.traditional: 主管第一次讓我負責重要會議。他說不必穿太正式，乾淨就好。那天鬧鐘還沒響，我就醒來了。我照主管說的，一再確認衣服穿得夠不夠{1}，就提早到公司{2}會場。桌子放哪裡主管早就決定了，我只要搬桌子。沒想到會議一開始，我就把給客人{3}的簡介搞錯了。主管沒批評我，先說笑話逗客人開心，等大家都覺得比較{4}了，才請同事換資料。會後主管說不怪我，我卻一直覺得是自己的錯，沒辦法{5}自己。他說：「新人多多少少都會緊張，{6}這是你第一次。」
passage.simplified: 主管第一次让我负责重要会议。他说不必穿太正式，干净就好。那天闹钟还没响，我就醒来了。我照主管说的，一再确认衣服穿得够不够{1}，就提早到公司{2}会场。桌子放哪里主管早就决定了，我只要搬桌子。没想到会议一开始，我就把给客人{3}的简介搞错了。主管没批评我，先说笑话逗客人开心，等大家都觉得比较{4}了，才请同事换资料。会后主管说不怪我，我却一直觉得是自己的错，没办法{5}自己。他说：「新人多多少少都会紧张，{6}这是你第一次。」
passage.pinyin: Zhǔguǎn dì yī cì ràng wǒ fùzé zhòngyào huìyì. Tā shuō búbì chuān tài zhèngshì, gānjìng jiù hǎo. Nà tiān nàozhōng hái méi xiǎng, wǒ jiù xǐnglái le. Wǒ zhào zhǔguǎn shuō de, yízài quèrèn yīfu chuān de gòu bú gòu zhěngqí, jiù tízǎo dào gōngsī bùzhì huìchǎng. Zhuōzi fàng nǎlǐ zhǔguǎn zǎo jiù juédìng le, wǒ zhǐ yào bān zhuōzi. Méixiǎngdào huìyì yì kāishǐ, wǒ jiù bǎ gěi kèrén cānkǎo de jiǎnjiè gǎo cuò le. Zhǔguǎn méi pīpíng wǒ, xiān shuō xiàohuà dòu kèrén kāixīn, děng dàjiā dōu juéde bǐjiào qīngsōng le, cái qǐng tóngshì huàn zīliào. Huì hòu zhǔguǎn shuō bú guài wǒ, wǒ què yìzhí juéde shì zìjǐ de cuò, méi bànfǎ yuánliàng zìjǐ. Tā shuō: “Xīnrén duōduōshǎoshǎo dōu huì jǐnzhāng, bìjìng zhè shì nǐ dì yī cì.”
passage.english: For the first time, my supervisor put me in charge of an important meeting. He said there was no need to dress too formally; clean was enough. That day I woke up before my alarm even rang. Following what my supervisor said, I checked again and again that my clothes were neat enough, then went to the company early to set up the venue. Where the tables went, my supervisor had decided long before; I only had to move them. Unexpectedly, as soon as the meeting began, I mixed up the brochures meant for the clients' reference. My supervisor did not criticize me. He first told a joke to amuse the clients, and only once everyone felt a bit more relaxed did he ask a colleague to swap the papers. After the meeting he said he did not blame me, but I kept feeling it was my fault and could not forgive myself. He said, "Newcomers are always more or less nervous. After all, this is your first time."

passage.traditional: 我去年開始領導銷售小組。剛開始大家只顧自己的事，工作安排得很{1}：有人忙不過來，有人沒事做。有一次，一位同事只說要送桌子，沒說要送哪一張，我們就搞錯了，差點失去這位客人，我才發現問題出在{2}上。有的同事很少開口，我本來以為他們不關心，聽了他們的說明，才{3}他們的想法。後來我照能力重新分配{4}，上班時間不變，只是負責的事變了。我也每星期舉行小組{5}，讓大家說說遇到的困難。以前我們總是比別組差，今年賣的桌子跟第一名一樣多，終於{6}了他們。

passage.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián kāishǐ lǐngdǎo xiāoshòu xiǎozǔ. Gāng kāishǐ dàjiā zhǐ gù zìjǐ de shì, gōngzuò ānpái de hěn hùnluàn: yǒu rén máng bú guòlái, yǒu rén méi shì zuò. Yǒu yí cì, yí wèi tóngshì zhǐ shuō yào sòng zhuōzi, méi shuō yào sòng nǎ yì zhāng, wǒmen jiù gǎo cuò le, chàdiǎn shīqù zhè wèi kèrén, wǒ cái fāxiàn wèntí chū zài gōutōng shàng. Yǒu de tóngshì hěn shǎo kāikǒu, wǒ běnlái yǐwéi tāmen bù guānxīn, tīng le tāmen de shuōmíng, cái lǐjiě tāmen de xiǎngfǎ. Hòulái wǒ zhào nénglì chóngxīn fēnpèi rènwù, shàngbān shíjiān bú biàn, zhǐshì fùzé de shì biàn le. Wǒ yě měi xīngqí jǔxíng xiǎozǔ huìyì, ràng dàjiā shuō shuo yùdào de kùnnán. Yǐqián wǒmen zǒngshì bǐ bié zǔ chà, jīnnián mài de zhuōzi gēn dì yī míng yíyàng duō, zhōngyú gǎnshàng le tāmen.
passage.english: Last year I began leading a sales team. At first everyone only looked after their own work, and the work was arranged chaotically: some people could not keep up while others had nothing to do. Once a colleague only said a table had to be delivered, not which one, so we got it wrong and nearly lost that client; only then did I realize the problem lay in communication. Some colleagues rarely spoke up; I had thought they did not care, and only after hearing them explain did I understand how they saw things. Then I reassigned tasks according to ability; working hours stayed the same, only what each person was in charge of changed. I also held a team meeting every week so everyone could talk about the difficulties they ran into. We always used to do worse than the other teams; this year we sold as many tables as the top team and finally caught up with them.

text.traditional:
歡迎各位來本公司面試！抵達之前，請先看下面的說明：
時間：下星期六上午九點開始，請在八點半之前抵達三樓會議室。
資料：面試銷售工作的人，請帶過去的工作資料給主管參考；面試設計工作的人，除了工作資料以外，還要帶三張自己畫的木頭家具設計圖。
內容：包含個人介紹和小組任務討論。不必穿正式的衣服，乾淨整齊就好。
通知：面試之後五天以內會寄電子郵件通知結果。薪水和福利（包含交通費、每年一次健康檢查）只在錄取通知裡詳細說明，面試當天不回答這方面的問題。

臺中有一家家具工廠，做木頭家具已經做了三十年。過去，老老闆一個人管全公司的事。儘管他做的桌子和椅子品質很好，可是他的觀念很傳統，往往只相信自己的經驗，很少聽員工的意見，甚至把別家公司看成敵人。後來年輕客人喜歡的樣式變了，工廠卻沒跟著調整。眼看生意越來越差，老老闆相當擔心。
五年前，老老闆的女兒張小姐回到臺中，開始領導這家工廠。她沒把父親過去的做法都換掉，但決定實行新制度：把員工分成設計和銷售兩個小組，每星期舉行會議討論新產品，也把客人的反應整理起來給大家參考。剛開始，一些老同事不理解為什麼要聽年輕人的看法，工廠變得很混亂，還有人差一點離開。

text.english:
In Taichung there is a furniture factory that has been making wooden furniture for thirty years. In the past, the old owner ran everything in the whole company by himself. Even though the tables and chairs he made were of high quality, his mindset was very traditional: he tended to trust only his own experience, rarely listened to employees' opinions, and even viewed other companies as enemies. Later, the styles young customers liked changed, yet the factory did not adjust with them. Watching business get worse and worse, the old owner was deeply worried.
Five years ago, the old owner's daughter, Ms. Zhang, returned to Taichung and began leading the factory. She did not discard all of her father's past ways, but decided to carry out a new system: dividing staff into design and sales teams, holding weekly meetings to discuss new products, and organizing customers' responses for everyone's reference. At first, some senior colleagues could not understand why they had to listen to young people's views; the factory became quite chaotic, and some nearly left.
Ms. Zhang did not lose her temper; instead she humbly asked the senior colleagues to teach her furniture-making craft, while letting younger colleagues create new styles. Gradually, everyone realized that regardless of age, they were all devoting themselves to the same enterprise and became willing to cooperate to the best of their ability. Today, the old factory's business is much better than before, and Ms. Zhang hopes everyone in the workplace keeps learning from one another.

text.traditional:
很多剛畢業的年輕人進職場之前，都以為只要專業能力強、順利通過面試，自己的事業就會很順利。其實，許多企業主管發現，不少相當優秀的新同事，上班之後往往會遇到挫折，問題卻不在專業方面，是在跟同事的相處上。
一些能力很強的人，太相信自己的看法。同事提出建議時，他們不是隨便聽聽，就是批評別人的想法不夠實際。碰到困難時，他們也只顧自己的表現，甚至把同小組的人看成敵人，破壞了大家的關係。儘管這些人自己很努力，但全組的人如果不能互相理解、配合，再好的計畫也不能順利實行。
相反地，真正在企業裡得到肯定的員工，會盡最大的力量完成自己的任務，做事細心，也願意謙虛地向同事請教。不論是領導小組還是協助同事，他們都願意花時間了解別人的想法，為大家創造一個容易溝通的環境。因此，想在職場上成功的人，除了加強專業能力以外，也該學會跟同事合作。

一些能力很强的人，太相信自己的看法。同事提出建议时，他们不是随便听听，就是批评别人的想法不够实际。碰到困难时，他们也只顾自己的表现，甚至把同小组的人看成敌人，破坏了大家的关系。尽管这些人自己很努力，但全组的人如果不能互相理解、配合，再好的计划也不能顺利实行。
相反地，真正在企业里得到肯定的员工，会尽最大的力量完成自己的任务，做事细心，也愿意谦虚地向同事请教。不论是领导小组还是协助同事，他们都愿意花时间了解别人的想法，为大家创造一个容易沟通的环境。因此，想在职场上成功的人，除了加强专业能力以外，也该学会跟同事合作。
text.pinyin: Hěn duō gāng bìyè de niánqīngrén jìn zhíchǎng zhīqián, dōu yǐwéi zhǐyào zhuānyè nénglì qiáng, shùnlì tōngguò miànshì, zìjǐ de shìyè jiù huì hěn shùnlì. Jǐnguǎn zhèxiē rén zìjǐ hěn nǔlì, dàn quán zǔ de rén rúguǒ bù néng hùxiāng lǐjiě, pèihé, zài hǎo de jìhuà yě bù néng shùnlì shíxíng. Yīncǐ, xiǎng zài zhíchǎng shàng chénggōng de rén, chúle jiāqiáng zhuānyè nénglì yǐwài, yě gāi xuéhuì gēn tóngshì hézuò.
text.english:
Before entering the workplace, many recent graduates assume that as long as their professional skills are strong and they pass the interview smoothly, their career will go smoothly. In fact, many company supervisors find that quite a few highly capable new colleagues often run into setbacks after starting work—not in terms of professional skills, but in getting along with coworkers.
Some very capable people trust their own views too much. When colleagues make suggestions, they either listen casually or criticize others' ideas as unrealistic. When difficulties arise, they look out only for their own performance, even viewing teammates as enemies and ruining everyone's relationships. Even though such people work hard themselves, if the whole team cannot understand and cooperate with one another, even the best plan cannot be carried out smoothly.
By contrast, employees who truly earn approval in an enterprise do their very best to complete their own tasks, work carefully, and are willing to modestly ask colleagues for advice. Whether leading a team or assisting colleagues, they are willing to spend time understanding what others think, creating an environment where everyone can communicate easily. Therefore, anyone who wants to succeed in the workplace should, besides strengthening their professional ability, also learn to work with colleagues.
